messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGE fired for service=runtime-queue-proxy severity=high — queue depth > 95th percentile and avg wait > 2.5s for 5m. Pager: pagerduty, Escalation policy: infra-oncall.

pagerduty: Incident INC-2023-847 triggered and routed to maria (on-call). Link: https://pd/redwood/INC-2023-847

maria: Acking — on it. Investigating queue-proxy + autoscaler. grabbing recent HPA and queue metrics.

maria: Quick telemetry: queue-proxy queue-length metric spiked to ~11k, request-scheduler lat p95 3.1s, autoscaler desired=3 current=3, cpu/util ~30% but backlog > threshold. Looks like autoscaler not scaling on queue length signals.

kai: +1 seeing the spike on prometheus: query: sum(queue_prox_queue_length{env=prod}) by (pod) — a ton of small sources sending high-concurrency bursts. Could be a sudden customer load or a retry loop.

jon: Any recent deploy to runtime or autoscaler? I see a canary earlier but it passed. No config change to HPA/scale-controller in last 2h.

maria: No deploys from my side. Checking autoscaler logs.

incident-bot: Log excerpt (autoscaler):
```
2024-06-21T12:03:15Z INFO evaluating scaling signal: queue_length=10234, desired_from_policy=3
2024-06-21T12:03:15Z WARN scaling inhibited: cooldown active for deployment/runtime-queue-proxy
2024-06-21T12:03:15Z ERROR scale up failed: insufficient node capacity in nodepool=prod-gpu-pool
```

maria: OK there it is — cooldown + nodepool capacity. HPA wants to scale but nodepool can't accept new pods and the scale-controller is backing off.

kai: We should open emergency burst. Options: 1) manually scale nodepool (gcloud/eks) 2) scale replica count manually to drain queue across existing nodes (might OOM) 3) divert traffic to another region/dedicated.

jon: If nodepool is full, manual replica increase won't schedule. Need nodes. I can spin up a small nodepool surge in the region — takes ~3-6m to join. Do we want to do that?

maria: Yes, please. Jon, create a temporary nodepool scaled to +6 nodes labeled autoscale-emergency. Also open a rollback in case autoscaler misbehaves. I'll start mitigation meanwhile: enable request-shed low-priority routes and apply stricter admission throttling for non-critical customers.

jon: Running command now:
```
# gcloud example
gcloud container node-pools create emergency-burst-1 --cluster=redwood-prod --machine-type=n1-highmem-8 --num-nodes=6 --zone=us-central1-a --labels=emergency=yes
```

incident-bot: pagerduty update: INC-2023-847 acknowledged by maria at 2024-06-21T12:05:10Z.

maria: Applying admission throttles: updating request-scheduler config map to drop or rate-limit unauthenticated/low-tier routes. Patch:
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap request-scheduler --patch '{"data":{"throttle_policy":"tiered:gold=unlimited,silver=50rps,bronze=5rps"}}'
```

kai: Seeing immediate drop in ingress to queue-proxy from low-tier customers — good. p95 latency trending down from 3.1s to 2.1s. Queue length still high but growth rate reduced.

maria: Jon, any ETA on nodes?

jon: Nodepool create succeeded; nodes joining. kubelet registration happening. Scheduling backlog decreasing as new nodes accept pods.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: New nodes registered: 6. Cluster autoscaler disabled for emergency-burst-1 (manual pool).

maria: Manually bumped replicas for runtime-queue-proxy to 9 to match new capacity:
```
kubectl -n runtime scale deploy/runtime-queue-proxy --replicas=9
```

kai: New pods scheduling and becoming Ready. queue length halting and starting to drain. p95 now ~1.4s.

jon: Note — autoscaler still in cooldown and will not react until cooldown expires. We should record this in the postmortem: autoscaler cooldown + nodepool capacity edge case.

maria: Working on customer impact: post-checking error rates. A small % of requests received 429s between 12:01-12:07 for bronze tier. No major enterprise customers affected. Raising status page to "degraded performance" for inference API for ~30m window.

sre-handoff-bot: Handoff reminder — next on-call is kai in 25m. 

maria: Preparing incident summary for PD and status page:
- root cause: autoscaler unable to scale due to nodepool capacity + cooldown; queue length rose, causing request backlog and higher latencies.
- mitigation: created emergency nodepool (+6), scaled replicas to 9, tightened admission throttles to reduce low-tier load, drained backlog.
- customer impact: bronze tier saw increased 429/slow responses for ~6m; overall p95 latency spike for runtime.

kai: Recommend action items post-incident:
- relax cooldown or add queue-based scale signal to bypass cooldown when backlog > X
- ensure cluster has emergency burst pool or rapid node allocation path (pre-warmed)
- add synthetic probes for queue length to alert earlier and separate PD path for node capacity vs backlog.

jon: I'll attach the commands and logs to the PD incident. Also creating a follow-up ticket to provision a pre-warmed nodepool.

maria: Good. I'm closing the PD incident now but leave the Slack thread open until metrics stable.

pagerduty: Incident INC-2023-847 resolved by maria at 2024-06-21T12:25:22Z — status: resolved. Notes: emergency nodepool created, replicas scaled, admission throttles applied.

maria: Metrics stable for 10m. queue length back to baseline, p95 ~500ms. Closing thread in 10. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

kai: :wave: filing postmortem draft and linking here.

jon: I'll teardown emergency nodepool in 10m and revert manual replica count to autoscaler-managed state.

sre-handoff-bot: Handoff: Kai is now primary oncall.

maria: Archived logs and action items posted to INC-2023-847. End thread.
